scope: Proposition 2.2 (Renewal factorization) of the manuscript “Renewal and changes of law for critical honeycomb walks” (preprints/Renewal-and-changes-of-law-for-critical-honeycomb-walks-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d179fa55e4b82fed), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 6-7. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The masses p(γ) sum to one. If H, L, X, D denote respectively the height, visited-vertex length, signed transverse displacement and Euclidean diameter of an irreducible, then, for s > 0 and u ≥ 0, b(s, u) := ∑︂ h≥0 ∑︂ γ∈Bh ρL(γ) e−sh−uL(γ) = 1 1 − Epe−sH−uL . 6 In particular b(s, 0) ≍ s−3/4 as s ↓ 0. Under independent successive samples from p, Bh is the probability that some renewal occurs at height h.
